observed_images.label: The Sun in extreme ultraviolet
observed_images.credits: Courtesy of NASA/SDO and the AIA, EVE, and HMI science teams.
observed_images.interpretation: AIA 171 angstrom extreme ultraviolet reveals structure in the solar corona. Gold is the channel's false color, not the Sun's visible-light appearance.
observed_images.derivation: Original NASA SDO archive JPEG bytes retained unchanged, including embedded instrument and UTC caption. Full image visually inspected at acquisition. No crop, recoloring, generated fill or geometric remapping.
observed_images.limits: Archived educational browse still; not live or synchronized to the model. Display the full image in its original camera plane. No model overlay, global sphere wrapping, heliographic coordinate measurement or calibrated analysis. NASA SDO browse products require principal-investigator consent for scientific analysis or publication.

mapped_references.label: NASA satellite clouds and surface
mapped_references.color_interpretation: MODIS corrected-reflectance display RGB; not a cloud-only layer or calibrated albedo.
mapped_references.limitations: Dated Terra-priority/Aqua-fallback MODIS corrected-reflectance composite; different overpass times on the same UTC day. Surface and clouds, not simultaneous or live weather. Seams and remaining gaps are retained; no global completeness claim. Missing areas show the historical land map. Night lights are a separate annual cloud-free reference, not cloud-attenuated live emissions.
mapped_references.derivation: Preserve each original decoded RGB value. Set alpha255 for published mask Data(0,0,0,0), alpha0 for NoData(202,170,86,255). Reject other classes. No inferred cloud pixels or black-color threshold. Same-date Aqua fills only pixels where Terra's published mask is NoData and Aqua's mask is Data. Retain Terra at overlap, including valid black RGB. No averaging, cloud motion extrapolation or interpolation. Both missing stays transparent. Coverage: {"valid_pixels": 1909254, "no_data_pixels": 187898, "total_pixels": 2097152, "terra_pixels": 1848641, "aqua_fill_pixels": 60613}

mapped_references.label: MESSENGER monochrome surface reference
mapped_references.credits: NASA / Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory / Carnegie Institution of Washington / USGS
mapped_references.observation_label: 2012-03-29 to 2015-04-30; multiple images and illumination geometries
mapped_references.color_interpretation: Monochrome NAC and WAC 750 nm reflectance mosaic; stretched grayscale, not visible RGB color or an unlit albedo texture. Source JPEG has no embedded ICC profile; browser RGB display interpretation is a local assumption.
mapped_references.limitations: Official browse is natively 1024x512; no invented higher-resolution detail. Photometric normalization retains topographic shading; global lighting is not recalibrated albedo. USGS describes no large gaps, not perfect coverage. JPEG has no independent nodata mask. Local display mask withholds |latitude| > 85 degrees to avoid severe polar seam/shading artifacts; this is a conservative display restriction, not the mission coverage boundary.

mapped_references.label: Viking colorized surface reference
mapped_references.observation_label: Viking mission-era composite (1976-1980); exact contributing dates unavailable; USGS publication 2009-02-02
mapped_references.color_interpretation: Viking color mosaic warped onto the MDIM 2.1 monochrome map. Colorized reference appearance, not simultaneous natural-color photography or calibrated albedo. Source JPEG has no embedded ICC profile; browser RGB display interpretation is a local assumption.
mapped_references.limitations: The source raster has slight outer latitude/longitude padding. Preserve the supplied bounds; do not assume exact -180/+180 pixel edges. Zero is declared nodata in each source band; JPEG compression and mosaic seams limit exact per-pixel validity. No inference of current dust, polar-cap season, or weather.

mapped_references.label: Magellan radar surface beneath clouds
mapped_references.observation_label: Magellan imaging cycles 1-3, September 1990 to September 1992; multiple observations
mapped_references.color_interpretation: Single-band radar backscatter in grayscale. This depicts surface structure beneath opaque clouds, not visible-light terrain colors, cloud structure, elevation, or calibrated optical albedo. Original 8-bit grayscale TIFF has no embedded ICC profile; equal-channel browser RGB is a display assumption.
mapped_references.limitations: Incomplete radar coverage: black source gaps are masked, not interpreted as terrain. Conservative source-zero mask plus BOX area downsampling excludes pixels whose support contains withheld values; no gap inpainting or colorization was performed. Actual raster extent is slightly short of a full360degrees; source UV outside[0,1] is unavailable and must not silently repeat to assert coverage. Radar backscatter depends on illumination/viewing geometry and material; visual lighting is illustrative and must not imply optical reflectance.

mapped_references.label: Contrast-enhanced Hubble cloud reference
mapped_references.credits: NASA / ESA / HST OPAL team; data archived by STScI MAST
mapped_references.color_interpretation: F631N red, F502N green, F395N blue; slight contrast enhancement. Arbitrarily scaled display TIFF; not calibrated I/F or a true-color calibration. RGB TIFF has no embedded ICC profile; browser RGB display interpretation is a local assumption.
mapped_references.limitations: Source contains moon/shadow transit residuals; transient bright/dark points are not permanent surface features.
